feed.title: Vx
feed.subtitle: Notes on building Vx, a heterogeneous-systems programming language.

entry.title: Many short tapes
entry.summary: C, C++, Rust, Java and Python define themselves against an abstract machine with one unbounded memory, which is Turing's tape. Real machines have many memories, each bounded, disaggregated, and addressable by some processors and not others. Vx describes the machine as a finite graph of memories and checks capacity and routing at compile time.

entry.title: float * of C/C++/Rust Fails to Distinguish Host DRAM from GPU HBM
entry.summary: malloc and cudaMalloc return memory with different readers and different sizes, and C, C++ and Rust give both the same type. Libraries such as Thrust, SYCL and cudarc each built the missing type and lose it at every raw pointer. Vx makes the memory space part of the type, so device memory cannot be passed, assigned or read as host memory.

entry.title: Asking the other compiler
entry.summary: Two impls of one trait for one type collided on a single mangled name, and choosing between them looked like a language design decision. Compiling the same program in Rust showed that Rust decides nothing: it infers the argument's type first, and then exactly one impl applies. The untyped literal case it settles with a blunt fallback to i32, which Vx already had.

entry.title: The library that only worked on the machine that built it
entry.summary: Vx 0.0.1 shipped on 10 September and could not run hello-world on any machine except the one that built it. Both macOS libraries recorded the release runner's own directory as their identity, and the release smoke test passed because it ran on that runner. Three more bugs were hiding behind it.

entry.title: The 43 gigabytes that are never there
entry.summary: Add up every tensor a Llama-2-7B prefill puts on the GPU and you get 58.93 GiB, which does not fit a 40 GiB A100. The tensors resident at the same time peak at 15.94 GiB, and the 42.99 GiB difference is larger than the card. Vx computes the peak from the program's block structure and a declared machine model, at compile time.

entry.title: Tiles, without a tile type
entry.summary: Can Vx be used for tile-based GPU programming, the way NVIDIA's cuTile is? A block loop, a tensor in Memory::SMEM and two barriers already compile to PTX with shared storage and bar.sync. What Vx adds is that the tile's memory space is part of its type and its shared-memory budget is a compile error; what it lacks is everything that makes a tile a value.

entry.title: The compiler bugs we found by writing Vx's core library
entry.summary: A week ago Vx had no core library. Now it has six modules of it, a random-number library, and the compiler fixes that writing them forced, a method that dispatched differently between runs among them. Every line is Vx, with no extern in it.

entry.title: The NUMA that wasn't there
entry.summary: A CPU's NUMA domains are the same relation as two GPUs on a node, so modelling them needed no new machinery. The compiler predicted a remote access costs 2.26x a local one and the hardware said 2.35x — after a day of measurements taken on a machine that reports two NUMA nodes it does not have.

entry.title: What a pointer forgets
entry.summary: A function stages a tensor to the GPU and returns it. In C++ the return type is float * and the fact is gone at the boundary. In Vx the memory space is part of the type, so the return type carries it.

entry.title: Vx 0.0.1: placement in the type system
entry.summary: The first Vx release. What the compiler checks, what it runs on, and the parts that are honestly not built yet.
